podcast.body: Conceived by Trent Reznor as a soundtrack to a potential movie or TV series, this album presents a fictionalized, alternate future history of the United States after 2007, where the government becomes increasingly repressive. The promotion of the album involved intricate, multi-dimensional marketing, including online components and a massive worldwide scavenger hunt for clues that actively involved fans. The project is compelling enough that HBO and BBC are collaborating to create a sci-fi miniseries based on the record, involving significant investment and major players. "Night Resonor conceived everything as a soundtrack to a movie or a TV series that might get made."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released independently in 2007 through Trent Reznor's company, The Null Corporation, as part of his "rogue" approach to releasing music independently, sometimes for free. "His year zero album from 2007... were all released independently through Trent's company called The Null Corporation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was Nine Inch Nails' fifth studio album and also an alternate reality game (ARG). The project incorporated concepts that offered a scathing critique of the US government and predicted a fundamentalist democracy by 2022. The ARG involved multiple websites, pre-recorded phone messages, emails, videos, murals, and MP3s. As part of its promotion, USB sticks containing clues and music were left in places like bathrooms at Nine Inch Nails concerts, and clues were also integrated into merchandise sold at these gigs. "This was both the fifth studio album for 9-H nails and an alternate reality game."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: ARG Launch Album
podcast.body: This album is considered one of the most brilliant records of the 21st century, primarily due to its innovative marketing strategy rather than solely its musical content. The release was an incredibly complex undertaking that integrated an Alternate Reality Game (ARG), making risky assumptions about human behavior. Clues were intricately buried in various unconventional places, which fans successfully discovered and connected. The album's launch commenced on February 7, 2007, in Lisbon, Portugal, coinciding with the first night of a European tour, and was officially released on April 17, 2007. The physical CD itself held a hidden clue: if the black label was warmed by a hand, binary codes would appear, leading to more secret websites. Upon its release, the album was uploaded to peer-to-peer networks, prompting immediate global analysis by fans searching for embedded clues, including a mysterious toll-free number.
